## Deployment status: RC6 is live on one chain

The generation this documentation describes is **RC6**. As of **2026-08-19** it is deployed on
**Robinhood Chain (4663)**, its factory there holds `PUBLIC`, and that chain accepts **ordinary
creator launches**. Every RC6 contract on it is source-verified on the chain's own explorer.

It is **not deployed on Ethereum (1), Base (8453) or BNB Smart Chain (56)**. Those three are
configured — they have chain profiles, the bundle format accepts them, the kit validates against
them — and configured is not deployed. **No date is set for any of them**, and nothing on this page
should be read as one.

### This repository still publishes no RC6 address, and that is not the same statement

Two facts, and they currently point in different directions:

- **Whether a chain accepts your launch** is a property of that chain's factory. On 4663 it is
  `PUBLIC`. You can read that yourself: `launchAccessState()` on the factory.
- **Whether this repository prints an address for it** is a publication decision, governed by one
  rule — *an address is published only from a deployment package that was actually broadcast* — and
  enforced by one command, `npm run kit:deployments:sync`. Nobody hand-types an address into this
  repository, including now.

The launchpad's deployment package for chain 4663 has not been regenerated as signed+broadcast since
the broadcast, so the sync command has nothing to publish from and declines. The result is a live
chain with no address in this kit. That is the rule working: the launch-access fact came from the
chain, and the address did not get invented to match it.

**So read the RC6 addresses off `robinhoodchain.blockscout.com`** until the sync publishes them, and
verify the source there rather than trusting any list — including a future one here.

`relics status` says all of this in one screen, per generation and per chain, and marks the
Robinhood row `PUBLIC` with the address column empty. It is generated from the same records this
page is, so the two cannot drift.

If you are holding addresses from an earlier version of this documentation, they are **RC5**
addresses. RC5 is the previous generation — real, source-verified, and still `PREPARED` on all three
chains it lives on. It is not what an RC6 bundle launches through.

Robinhood Chain is the only chain RC6 exists on, and it is open to ordinary creator launches. Ethereum, Base and BNB Smart Chain are configured in the bundle format and the chain profiles, and RC6 is not deployed on any of them; configured is not deployed, and no date is announced for any of the three. The chains now differ in launch state as well as in the quote leg, so read the row rather than assuming they match.

<!-- /generated:chains -->

Two things that table is deliberately not saying.

**The chains are no longer interchangeable, and `PUBLIC` is one-way.** A factory starts in
`PREPARED` — its zero value, so it is closed from the block it is initialized — and moves to
`PUBLIC` exactly once, when the upgrade authority calls `openPublicLaunches()`. Nothing returns it
to `PREPARED`, and when it opens, the pre-public canary entrypoint stops working entirely, so no
privileged creation path outlives the opening. Robinhood Chain has made that transition. The other
three have no factory to make it with.

**BNB is configured, and configured is not deployed.** Chain 56 carries a full chain profile — WBNB
as the wrapped native, its own gas budget, its own buy-and-entomb accumulation design — and no RC6
contracts. Presence in the schema, the kit, the SDK and the chain config is not a deployment, and no
reader-facing surface may claim the chain-56 buy-and-entomb half is active, converting, or settled.

On chain 56, never print "WETH" or "ETH". The settlement token is WBNB and gas is paid in BNB. The
symbol comes from the chain's own profile, through an accessor that **throws on an unknown chain
rather than returning a default** — because that default was correct on every chain that existed
when it was written and silently wrong on the first one that followed.

## The kit mirrors RC5; the product you will launch through is RC6

This is the sharpest edge in the repository and it deserves its own heading.

The creator kit in `packages/` records a `PROTOCOL_RELEASE_COMPATIBILITY` string, and the surface it
mirrors is the RC5 parameter surface — because RC5 is the generation that is actually deployed.
Meanwhile the documentation you are reading describes RC6, because RC6 is the generation a public
creator launch will run through.

What that means in practice:

- **A `.relics` bundle is a description of a project, not of a protocol release.** Its manifest,
  digests, art binding and market mapping are the same artifact either way. Building and validating
  a bundle today is real work that is not wasted.
- **A bundle never states which contracts are deployed at which addresses.** `runtimeCodeHash` and
  `scriptPointer` are chain facts and are always `null` in a bundle, refused by name if filled in.
  That is exactly what keeps a bundle valid across a generation change.
- **The kit's exported ADDRESS table is still RC5-only.** `relics status` reports both generations
  and marks Robinhood Chain `PUBLIC` under RC6, but the RC6 address entries are empty for the reason
  above. Read a printed address as RC5 unless the row says otherwise.
- **Where the two generations differ in behaviour, this documentation is the RC6 answer.** The hook
  permission mask, the dynamic pool fee, the launch-protection election, the disabled fixed-price
  mode, and metadata-at-birth are all RC6 behaviour and all differ from RC5.

The version surface and the address record are updated together, by the sync procedure below, as
each chain is broadcast.

## How to verify rather than trust

On Robinhood Chain there is now something to verify, and you should. These are the checks that mean
something — each one a fact you can reproduce, rather than a posture somebody asserted:

- **Source verification on the chain's own explorer**, for every deployed contract. Read the runtime
  bytecode against the published source before relying on any description of it, including this page.
- **Runtime codehashes**, compared against the release artifact. A codehash match is checkable; a
  description is not.
- **The hook's address bits.** `address & 0x3FFF` must equal the mask in
  [02 — What a launch produces](02-what-a-launch-produces.md). A hook at an address that does not
  encode its permissions cannot hold those permissions — Uniswap v4 will not call it.
- **The launch-access state**, read from the factory rather than from a document.
- **The immutability of the components you are relying on**, read from the EIP-1967 implementation
  slot: a proxy has one and a directly-deployed contract does not. See
  [11 — Governance and upgradeability](11-governance-and-upgradeability.md), which names which is
  which.

Internal fork work is real evidence about the conditions it tested — the launch path, fee
accounting, art binding and multi-quote settlement have been exercised against pinned forks. That is
a statement about those conditions and nothing wider.

## Known limits worth planning around

- **One chain, not four.** You can launch on Robinhood Chain (4663). On Ethereum, Base and BNB Smart
  Chain there is no RC6 factory to launch through, and building, validating and exporting a bundle
  is as far as you can go there.
- **The addresses are not in this kit yet.** See the deployment-status section: read them from the
  chain's explorer, and verify the source there.
- **One transaction, one gas budget.** A launch is a single atomic call and must fit under the
  chain's per-transaction gas cap. That is what forces the script byte budget in
  [04 — Constraints](04-constraints.md). Per-chain budgets must be measured independently rather
  than assumed from Ethereum's numbers.
- **The pool fee is dynamic, and the hook is the policy.** It is not a static tier you pick, and it
  is not a number an interface may print without reading. See
  [06 — Fees and revenue](06-fees-and-revenue.md) and
  [12 — Launch protection](12-launch-protection.md).
- **Fixed-price sale is withdrawn.** It is not "coming soon". The creator kit refuses a bundle that
  elects it at `relics validate` and `relics export`, and the deployed sale contract refuses it at
  launch for every caller. See [05 — The creator flow](05-creator-flow.md).
- **Genesis liquidity is single-sided.** There is no bid depth at launch until real buyers add quote
  currency. Nobody is obliged to buy.
- **Quote admission and WETH conversion are separate.** A quote can be enabled for launch before its
  route to WETH is proven; the buy-and-entomb half then remains quote-denominated and visibly
  pending.
- **Not everything is immutable, in either direction.** Your hook, the liquidity locker and the
  liquidity kernel have no upgrade path at all. Most of the protocol around them is upgradeable by a
  2-of-3 Safe with no timelock. Flattening that into one word is wrong whichever word you pick;
  [11 — Governance and upgradeability](11-governance-and-upgradeability.md) is the table.

## How to talk about this honestly

If you are writing about a project you intend to launch here:

- Name the chain. Say "RC6 is live on Robinhood Chain and open to creator launches there; it is not
  deployed on Ethereum, Base or BNB" — not "the launchpad is live", which reads as all four, and not
  "deployed on three chains", which is RC5.
- Do not turn a live chain into a roadmap. There is **no announced date** for Ethereum, Base or BNB,
  and "coming to Ethereum" is a claim this repository does not support.
- Cite a checkable fact — a verified source page, a runtime codehash, a hook address whose bits you
  can read — rather than a claim about who has or has not reviewed the code.
- Say "75% of collected LP fees" — not "0.75% of volume forever".
- Say "the platform share is denominated in the selected quote asset" — not "everything settles in
  WETH".
- Say "$RELICS bought and sent permanently to an entombment address; circulating supply falls,
  `totalSupply` stays fixed" — not "supply is burned". The deployed token has no burn path and no
  burn event occurs.
- Say "initialized price" for the price you open the pool at, and never call it a floor, a valuation,
  or a market price. Only trades make a market price.
- For launch protection, use the wording in [12 — Launch protection](12-launch-protection.md), which
  lists both the accurate claims and the ones that are false in either mode.

## Post-deployment sync — the procedure, not a promise

When a chain is broadcast, the deployment facts in this repository are **regenerated from the
production manifest**. Nobody hand-edits an address into a markdown table, because the hand-edited
copy is the one that survives the next redeploy.

This procedure has run for chain 4663 as far as it can: steps 4 through 8 are done and steps 1
through 3 are blocked, because the launchpad's deployment package for that chain has not been
regenerated as signed+broadcast. That is why the status is current and the addresses are absent.

The order matters: the machine-readable record moves first, then everything derived from it.

1. **Pin the deploy commit.** The production deployment manifest for each chain carries a
   `release.sourceCommit`. It is the commit the verified bytecode was built from, and every step
   below is meaningless without it.
2. **Regenerate the deployment record** in `packages/project-schema/src/deployments.js` from the
   production manifests (`launchpad/deployments/<chainId>.json`) — per-chain contract addresses, the
   release id, the freeze commit and the launch-access state. Never transcribe an address by hand;
   generate the file and diff it.
3. **Update the version surface** in `packages/project-schema/src/version.js`: bump
   `PROTOCOL_RELEASE_COMPATIBILITY` to the RC6 release identifier, and correct the doc comment that
   currently describes RC5 as the deployed generation. Bump `CREATOR_KIT_VERSION`. Bump
   `SCHEMA_VERSION` **only** if a manifest field changed meaning — a chain profile is not a bundle
   field.
4. **Update `docs/launchpad/protocol-facts.json`**: for each chain, set `rc6Status` and
   `publicCreatorLaunch` from the manifest and the on-chain `launchAccessState`, and set
   `deployment.status`, `deployment.statusSentence` and `deployment.addressesPublishedHere`. Every
   field carries the source it mirrors — update the source pointer too if it moved.
5. **Regenerate the docs and assets**: `node scripts/generate-doc-assets.mjs`. Every status banner,
   the chain table, the protection table, the launch-mode table, the immutability table and the fee
   curve update together, in one commit, from one edit.
6. **Verify no page drifted**: `node scripts/generate-doc-assets.mjs --check` must pass, and so must
   `npm run kit:economics` and `node scripts/check-links.mjs`.
7. **Re-verify the published claims against the chain, not the manifest.** For each chain: read
   `launchAccessState` from the factory; read `address & 0x3FFF` for a deployed art hook and confirm
   it equals the published mask; read one launched collection's `contractURI()` and confirm it is
   non-empty; confirm the source-verification status on the explorer. A manifest is a plan. The chain
   is the fact.
8. **Only then** update any prose that describes launch availability, and re-run the export manifest
   check.

Step 7 is the one that is tempting to skip and the one that catches a wrong deploy.

## Reporting a problem

If you find a security-relevant issue in anything published in this repository, follow
[`SECURITY.md`](../../SECURITY.md). Do not open a public issue with a working exploit path.
